x: Our sprinters proved very short of training, although Metcalfe, of the "Poly.," ran very well in the longer sprint.
Metcalfe, a very promising sprinter, and Wright gained us further points by finishing second and third in the 220 Yards.
220 Yds.—1, Broadbent (S.); 2, Metcalfe (N.); 3, Southey (N.) T. 24.6s. 440 Yds.—1, Jarlett (S.); 2, Pettit (N.); 3, Watts (S.).
Watts ran a good race to finish second to Ensor in the first string 440 Yards, and Metcalfe put up a good performance in running beyond his usual distance, to finish second in the second race.

The 220 Yards saw Metcalfe, the tall Poly. boy, just beat Bill Bowers, who had to be content with yet another second place. A good field also turned out for the 2 Miles race, and here again the North runners were more numerous than for the South.
Metcalfe of the Poly. gaining second place for the combined Belgrave-Polytechnic side. In the 2 Miles, however, our distance runners received a rude shock when H.

Wigley repeated his win in the 220, but this time Bowers moved up a place, with Metcalfe of the Poly. taking second place. Metcalfe, of the Poly, who are again assisting us this season. We had the individual winner of every track event and Frank Abberton, who was on leave, ran well to win the 2 Miles.
Metcalfe won the 220 Yards for us, while M.

Metcalfe took the furlong in 23.6s., being chased home by Brant, Harris, Molyneux and Vine. Watts scored a double by winning the 440 in 51.1s., with Bishop third, and 880 in 2m. 5.4s., with Brown third and Bishop fourth.

Where was the Brightwell strength and the Metcalfe flair in the one lap event? Then, even allowing the criminal handicap of altitude running, can we in any way equate Messrs Herriot, Taylor and Blinston with the Ibbotsons, Piries and Norrises of little more than a decade ago.
